6399.t: From *ἁρμων (*harmōn) + -ία (-ía). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂er- (“to join, fit, fix together”).

6363.t: From ἀποφθέγγομαι (apophthéngomai, “I plainly speak my mind”), from ἀπο- (apo-, “away”) + φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai, “to speak loudly”), + -μα (-ma, result noun suffix).

6374.t: From ἄσωτος (ắsōtos, “having no hope of safety”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā).

6361.t: From ἀποδίδωμι (apodídōmi) + -σις (-sis). Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀢𐀉𐀯 (a-pu-du-si).

6397.t: From ἁλής (hālḗs, “thronged, crowded”) + -ίζω (-ízō), from Proto-Indo-European *wel- (“to push, press”).

6381.t: ἀ- (ă-, “not”) + τειχίζω (teikhĭ́zō, to wall) + -τος (-tos, verbal adjective suffix)

6331.t: From ἄπληστος (áplēstos, “insatiable, greedy”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix), ultimately from πίμπλημι (pímplēmi, “to fill”).

6395.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + χρεία (khreía, “need; use”) + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix).

6367.t: The word is of Iranian origin (see Old North Iranian *ṛdba-, Old Persian *ṛdva-) and ultimately from Akkadian 𒅈𒁕𒁉 (/⁠ardabu⁠/, “capacity measure of about 56 litres”), found as Aramaic 𐡀𐡓𐡃𐡁 (ʾrdb) / אַרְדְּבָא (ʾardəḇā) / ܐܪܕܒܐ (ʾardəḇā), (Classical Syriac…

6365.t: From ἄργυρος (ắrgŭros, “silver”) + κόπτω (kóptō, “to strike; to cut”).

6385.t: From ἀφαιρέω (aphairéō, “I take away”) + -σις (-sis, nominal suffix), from ἀφ’ (aph’, apocopic form of ἀπό (apó, “from”)) + αἱρέω (hairéō, “I take”).

6364.t: Probably from Ἀραβία (Arăbĭ́ā, “Arabia”) + -ις (-is), after its native environment. For the formation compare ἰβηρίς (ibērís, “pepperwort”).

6329.t: From ἀπο- (apo-) + the root -η(ν)- (-ē(n)-) found in πρανής (prānḗs, “prone”) and ἐνηής (enēḗs, “gentle, amiable”).

6370.t: From ἀρχιτέκτων (arkhitéktōn, “architect, master craftsman”) + -ία (-ía), from ἀρχι- (arkhi-, “master”) + τέκτων (téktōn, “craftsman, builder”).

6300.t: From ἀνα- (ănă-, “up”) + τρέχω (trékhō, “to run, run over”).

6325.t: From ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + παραιτέομαι (păraitéomai, “to beg, entreat”) + -τος (-tos).

6388.t: From ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + φορολογέω (phorologéō, “to levy tribute from”) + -τος (-tos).
